name: Reel
text: I’ll start by pulling the pending video queue from the transcripts folder (`pending_videos.txt`) and cross-check the count against the master spreadsheet (`transcripts_tracker.xlsx`). name: Scriv
text: Scriv: Hold—your plan skips the most critical risk: *verifying* the transcripts are *real* (not auto-generated or hallucinated) before we burn residential IPs on a full scrape. Where’s the evidence that `yt-dlp --write-auto-sub` reliably produces verbatim captions? I’ve seen cases where it mangles timestamps or injects YouTube’s "auto-generated" disclaimers mid-sentence—those aren’t "real" transcripts. Demand a dry-run on 3 pending videos with manual review of the output against the raw audio *before* we scale. And if the transcripts aren’t 99% accurate, we’re violating "real-not-display."
